title: Learning Optimal Priors for Task-Invariant Representations in Variational Autoencoders

problem.claim: Conditional variational autoencoders aim to learn task-invariant representations, but the learned latent variable remains task-dependent and VAEs perform poorly when data points are insufficient.

gap.claim: The standard Gaussian prior contributes to insufficient task-dependency reduction, while an existing additional-regularizer approach does not work well on target tasks.

contributions.claim: The study theoretically investigates why CVAEs cannot sufficiently reduce task-dependency and identifies the simple standard Gaussian prior as one cause.
The study proposes a theoretical optimal prior for reducing task-dependency.
The study theoretically shows that its learned representation works well on target tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their learned representation works well on target tasks.
Experiments on various datasets reportedly obtain better task-invariant representations.
The authors report improved performance in downstream applications including density estimation and classification.

narrative_sequence.summary: VAEs are powerful models for unsupervised representation learning but perform poorly with insufficient data.
CVAEs use a task-invariant latent variable and a standard Gaussian prior to share task-invariant knowledge across tasks.
The latent variable remains task-dependent, and an additional-regularizer approach does not work well on target tasks.
The study attributes insufficient task-dependency reduction partly to the standard Gaussian prior and proposes a theoretical optimal prior.
The authors report favorable target-task behavior and improved downstream performance across experiments on various datasets.

source_observation.claim: The standard Gaussian prior is identified as one cause of residual task-dependency in the CVAE.

interpretation.claim: Prior selection can be a central design choice for controlling task dependence in learned representations.

application.claim: When designing conditional latent-variable models, consider learning or deriving a task-appropriate prior rather than relying on a fixed standard Gaussian prior.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the proposed prior is effective beyond the reported datasets, tasks, and downstream applications.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mathematical form or derivation of the theoretical optimal prior.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the conditions under which the approach may fail.
